articles.title: Diablo 5 vai ser lançado em 2029 | G1
articles.standfirst: Próximo capítulo do game de RPG vai mostrar mundo no qual o grande vilão Diablo venceu. Blizzard anunciou Amazonas como a nova classe jogável de 'Diablo 4'.
articles.summary: Durante a BlizzCon, a Blizzard confirmou o desenvolvimento de Diablo 5, o novo capítulo da franquia de RPG de ação, com estreia prevista para o outono de 2029.
articles.body:
A Blizzard anunciou neste sábado (12) o desenvolvimento de "Diablo 5" (ou "Diablo V", no original), com lançamento previsto para o outono de 2029.

A história do novo capítulo do RPG de ação deve se passar um século depois da trama de "Diablo 4", jogo de 2023 cujo DLC mais recente, "Lord of Hatred" , foi lançado em abril.

O anúncio foi feito na BlizzCon, convenção da desenvolvedora.

A empresa também divulgou a próxima classe de "Diablo 4" vão ser as Amazonas, previstas para a primeira metade de 2027.

O game vai ganhar um versão para Switch 2 nesta terça-feira (15).

O novo jogo vai ser lançado "com mais classes do que já tivemos em um 'Diablo' antes", segundo afirmou o diretor sênior do jogo, Joe Shelly, à revista "Esquire".

Entre elas, estão o Monge e o Caçador de Demônios, vistas pelas última vez em "Diablo 3", e a estreia do Plague Knight (o Cavaleiro da Praga, em tradução livre).

"Santuário (o mundo do game) não é um lugar feliz na maioria das vezes, mas 'Diablo 5' leva a outro nível. Você está vivendo em um mundo que foi dominado por Diablo. Ele senta no trono, a humanidade está destruída, e os próprios jogadores estão fugindo", falou Shelly.

"Nós estávamos, tipo, 'e se o Diablo ganhasse e nós tivéssemos de lutar por território com nossas próprias unhas?' Queríamos fazer um mundo mais sombrio que nunca, mas te dar uma razão para lutar por ele", disse a diretora de narrativa, Jennifer Helper.

articles.title: How a VFX Controversy Propelled the Strange Journey of Na Hong-Jin's Sci-Fi Blockbuster Hope
articles.summary: Ten years after The Wailing, director Na Hong-jin has returned with a wild alien movie that's been marketed to every corner of film fandom — and the effort is paying off.
articles.body:
By the time I sat down with Na Hong-jin and his translator at a way-too-big hotel conference room table across the street from Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con, the director and writer already had the biggest movie in Korea. His latest film, Hope, had set the year’s record for opening-weekend admissions in the country, accounting for 66% of all movie ticket sales . Yet he wasn’t reveling in the success for his first movie in 10 years.

“All I could think about was, ‘What's it going to look like next week or even a week after?’” said Na as he looked toward the imminent threat of The Odyssey and Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

And yeah, those near-generational behemoths might have knocked Hope off its two-week box office reign at the top of Korean cinema. But, much like the characters (aliens, especially) in the blistering, rip-roaring action sci-fi, Hope wouldn’t stay down for long. Before its release in the US this week, distributor Neon announced it would open in 1,500 theaters — the most a Korean film has had since Bong Joon-ho’s Oscar-winning Parasite — and on premium screens like 4DX. (Of the latter, a good chunk of showings have sold out in major cities.) In its first day in theaters, Hope made more than $1 million .

Hope — the most expensive Korean film to-date — is unlike anything else you’ll see this year. Starring Hwang Jung-min as a small-town police chief, Squid Game’s Jung Ho-yeon as a rookie cop, and Zo In-sung as a townie cowboy, the film is about aliens coming to Hope Harbor, a tiny town located right along the Demilitarized Zone between North and South Korea. The structure and pace of the film is fascinating, delivering one climax after another as Na examines the locals’ response to the aliens, and the tone is both super-serious and funny in a way that fits in with movies like Jordan Peele’s Nope or Zack Cregger’s Barbarian. Even in three-minute trailers, people were tickled by the amount of swearing, and in a nod to the discourse, Na confirmed the Korean word for “fuck” is featured 137 times .

Hope’s journey to theatrical release is as unique as the movie. First, it premiered in competition at this year’s Cannes Film Festival in May. This wasn’t Na’s first time showing work at the prestigious festival in the south of France — in fact, all three of his previous movies (The Chaser, The Yellow Sea, and The Wailing) screened there — but it was the first time he’d be competing for the big awards, like the Palm d’Or. Hope was the first Korean film to be in competition in four years; the last was Park Chan-wook’s Decision to Leave, which left the 2022 festival with the Best Director award in hand. It didn’t win, but its inclusion as an alien action blockbuster alongside the “serious” dramas more typical of the festival felt like a victory of its own. The general consensus around the early clips circulating online was a resounding “hell yeah.”

The reviews out of Cannes, however, were more polarizing. We gave it a 9 ; in his review, Siddhant Adlakha wrote that Hope “launches a gonzo sensory assault with an action-comedy-thriller saga of a small town beset by forces much larger than itself. [...] It’s a nonstop blast with the kind of low-to-the-ground vehicular and horseback action that’ll have you falling off the front of your seat.” Other critics were less enamored, specifically whomping on the CGI aliens; Indiewire , for example, slammed it as having some of the “worst creature effects this side of the Syfy Channel or The Mummy Returns.” Despite, or perhaps because of, the strong reactions, it was one of the buzziest movies at the festival.

The fuss around the aliens and their designs is not lost on Na, who’s been asked about the creatures in probably every single interview he’s given about this movie, and it’s not hard to figure out why it’s been such a curiosity. They were brought to life with real human actors — Michael Fassbender, Alicia Vikander, Taylor Russell, and Cameron Britton — using a unique motion-capture that rendered their performances on location in real time into the huge, odd-looking, shape-shifting creatures. The VFX work will certainly inspire opinions , but I found them kind of charming, especially in the jankier moments. In one scene, Vikander’s alien queen, which would not be out of place as an Awakened Being in the Claymore manga , lurches fluidly through a forest. In another, Fassbender’s alien warrior, in its Xenomorph-cheetah-dog form, sprints in a way that uncannily reminded me of the Forest Demon in a Smiling Friends Halloween episode. The off-putting nature of the beasts was intentional, both in terms of the bigger thematic picture of Hope and what Na was going for in having the “creatures fighting a battle in the daytime” with no dark corners or shadows for the CGI to hide behind, especially as the aliens get their asses kicked.

“The final look of the creatures in the movie that you see are over the course of six months; these creatures have gone through so many changes,” Na told me. “They are much more fucked up. They got a lot of injuries. In the end, it just didn't look the same as anything that we've seen before.”

Following Cannes, Hope was the centerpiece of the New York Asian Film Festival . Then, breaking from the festival circuit, it came to San Diego Comic-Con. And in the time in between his appearances in France and the US, Na went back into post-production , re-editing the film. The Cannes version, four-ish minutes longer than the final cut, was rushed out the door for the festival. Though he reworked scenes and the sound, the aliens remained largely untouched. He told the Comic-Con audience he had finished two weeks prior.

It’s not the only film to have made the jump from glitzy film festival to the massive nerd fan event — even this year, the out-of-competition Victorian Psycho starring Maika Monroe also came to both — but it is the first to have a dedicated panel in a gigantic room. (Dune: Part 1 would have completed the Venice to Comic-Con pipeline had SDCC 2021 not been a largely virtual event.) “It didn’t feel like Earth here,” Na said at the top of his panel in Ballroom 20, the second-largest space in the convention center. “I am aware that this is a very different space from traditional film festivals,” Na told me before taking the stage. “I honestly think that fandom-centered audiences would enjoy this movie a lot more. In fact, I think those are the kind of audiences who would enjoy all of my films a lot more.”

Na’s films do all have a genre sensibility that falls somewhere between, as the New Yorker’s Justin Chang described , “the aspirations of the art house and the pleasures of the grind house.” His first two films, 2008’s The Chaser and 2010’s The Yellow Sea, are gritty beat-em-up gangster movies. The Wailing, his 2016 breakout in the West that consistently lands on “best Korean movies”-type lists, was a blood-soaked shamanic mystery. Hope fits right alongside his violent folly-of-humans stories, where the aliens and humans aren’t so different.

“It's very heartbreaking and in the end you feel really, really bad for them,” Na told me. “At first you think these are aliens who just attack and hurt people. But then in the end, you realize that they're actually very pitiful creatures. And there's a metaphor to that element as well. This is the kind of story that we're trying to tell.”

articles.title: Zeverland Game Designer Discusses Its Unique Take on the Zombie Apocalypse
articles.body:
Survival crafting game Zeverland puts a unique spin on the genre by making its zombie apocalypse deceptively cute and allowing you to modify just about everything you can find.

That means you can duct tape a clothes iron to a tennis racket to turn it into a deadly weapon, or weld a camera to a baseball bat to electrify your attacks. You also have a vehicle you can customize however you want by welding other things to it and turning it into a mobile base. Attach a bed to give yourself somewhere to rest, or put ramming spikes on the front of your vehicle to mow down hordes of zombies.

After its most recent playtest in June, Zeverland underwent significant design changes based on player feedback. Originally announced as an open-world MMO where you could sabotage other players, it’s now shifted to focus on PvE co-op where you build, explore, and survive together with your friends, though solo play is also possible.

At gamescom, we got the chance to talk to Zeverland’s lead game designer Cecilia Pan about its focus on players helping each other, the creativity of players, the different gameplay systems it offers, and lots more.

Welcome, Cecilia. We know that Zeverland is a co-op survival game where you can smash, stash, and craft everything. But can you tell us a bit more about it?

Cecilia Pan: The game takes place a few months after a zombie apocalypse. The cities are still there, and you can enter all kinds of buildings, like police stations, hospitals, and convenience stores. You can interact with the objects inside in ways that feel natural, whether that means picking them up, putting them in your backpack, or combining them into weapons. We've already held two playtests, and we're currently planning to launch into Steam Early Access as early as Q1 next year.

Now one thing that stands out to me about Zeverland in general is this emphasis on assisting others versus, you know, fighting enemies. It seems like you're much more incentivizing people to work together. Can you talk to me about that?

Cecilia: Well, it's like this: When a natural disaster strikes, humanity ultimately always chooses to stand together and fight against it. We've played a lot of survival games ourselves, so we really wanted to make a game where, after disaster strikes, people use their own knowledge and creativity to solve survival problems, and eventually work together to take the world back from the zombies.

In most cases, co-op gameplay is designed around fixed storylines or specific bosses set by developers, which players must team up to conquer. What we want is a sandbox-style form of cooperation. There are endless ways to play the game, so players can choose whether or not they want to help each other. For example, vehicles need fuel. If you're driving down the road and come across another survivor, you can choose to stop and give them a can of gas so they can keep going. Of course, you can also choose not to. We want cooperation to come from the player's own choice.

And we don't want cooperation to stop once players have solved the basic problems of survival. We want to see whether they can work together to do something even bigger. Maybe they build a bridge across a river, set up ziplines between tall buildings, or find a way to restore power to a big city. Those are the kinds of experiences that require more players to come together and try something as a group.

That's really cool. I love the idea that you are kind of creating a bunch of different systems that, depending on how the players interact with them, you kind of incentivize that creativity. Now, you've talked about doing two public alpha play tests earlier, and I'm just curious: Are there any interesting stories, any favorite stories that you might have had during those alpha play tests?

Cecilia: During Playtest 2, I had a pretty interesting experience myself. I was driving down the road when I came across another player whose vehicle had broken down. I stopped and asked if they needed help. They told me they hadn't brought enough fuel, so their vehicle couldn't go any farther. I gave them some of the fuel I had saved, and we ended up becoming friends.

My second story goes like this: I once ran into a player who had built his entire home, including a personal bar, right on top of his vehicle. As the sun was setting, he parked on the side of the road and opened up a little mobile roadside bar. He and his NPC companion were playing music together, looking absolutely joyful, and I ended up joining them halfway through.

Lots of devs in our team really love this post-apocalyptic theme. While we were designing the game, teammates would often ask me things like, “Can I bring my screaming chicken?” or “Can I bring my little rubber duck?” In most cases, devs will tell players: “You need to complete a great mission.” But we want our world to be filled with small, familiar things from everyday life. Those little objects and little moments can remind players how valuable ordinary life is, and hopefully make them naturally want to come together and solve these survival problems.

Now, you talk a lot about how you kind of iterate on these different design decisions and things like that. You say Zeverland is a game with no limits. What are the kind of gameplay mechanics that you think best express that player creativity and freedom?

Cecilia: We currently have more than 6,000 interactive objects in the game. We use an ECS-based interaction system to make sure each object responds in a way that feels natural. Every object has its own material properties. Wood can burn, while metal can conduct electricity, and when it rains, that electricity can potentially spread even farther. An object's size and weight also determine whether it can fit in your backpack. If it can't, maybe you can pick it up and throw it instead, and that can deal damage. Once players understand these systems, they can use common sense and their own creativity to solve survival problems and overcome challenges in the game.

Yeah, I mean, let's just get right into weapon customization then. You kind of alluded to a lot of different systems, whether it be how they interact with elements, how they interact with the environment. How many different weapon customization options are there? And you've already been watching player behavior, so what are some of the weirdest weapons players have made?

Cecilia: For example, you can attach a little rubber duck to a weapon, and it'll make a weird noise when you hit a zombie. If you knock a zombie's head off, you can also attach that head to a weapon, and it might give the weapon a stun effect. You can also find everyday objects in houses, like an iron, and attach those to weapons. An iron, for example, might let you set zombies on fire. So there are a lot of fun combinations like that.

Do those kinds of customization options and player creativity also extend to the vehicles? Are there ways of customizing vehicles, and how do you kind of check out exploration in that regard?

Cecilia: We have a lot of different types of vehicles in the game, from bicycles that don't need fuel, to four-wheelers and pickup trucks. A pickup has space in the back where you can place furniture and basically turn it into a mobile base. You can also place objects on every surface of the containers, so you can decorate them almost like the walls of your own house. And if you want your vehicle to have more combat capability, you can also place traps or other defensive items on it.

Then I have one request, if it's not already in the game: Can you put a zombie head as a hood ornament on the tip of your truck?

I love that. Now let's move on to some of the key features. We’ve seen footage of players becoming infected and turning into a zombie. Can you walk me through that system? How does it work? Can you ever return to a normal human?

Cecilia: The idea of becoming a zombie came from a question our core team asks a lot during design discussions: “What if?” We started asking, what if getting infected didn't mean you simply died? What if you actually turned into a zombie instead? What would that experience look like? That's really how this system was born.

After you turn into a zombie, you still keep a lot of the combat abilities you had as a human, but your time may be limited. During that time, you need to find a way to turn back into a human. If time runs out, you may lose control, and the world will be left with a zombie carrying your previous character's name. Of course, you can also choose to spend those 15 minutes helping your friends with whatever you want to do together.

That's certainly one of the most clever examples I've seen of the kind of Souls-like “run back to your body and try and reclaim what you've lost.” That's really cool. Tell me about the different varieties: Is it just going to be four zombie types? Is there a plan to include different types of zombies in the future that you can kind of build on? And also, can I infect other humans?

Cecilia: Since we're targeting Early Access next year, our priority right now is to make the human experience as strong as possible. So for the moment, players only have these four options. In the future, we'd like to expand this system and make the zombie experience much richer. That could include some of the things you mentioned, but those would probably come sometime after Early Access.

We're nearly out of time, but I've got to know, especially with people who are interested in how this game is going to evolve, if there's anything you had to tell your community there, what do you have to say about the future of Zeverland?

Cecilia: After Playtest 2 ended, we gathered a lot of player feedback showing that players really want their own dedicated worlds with friends. In response, we are launching private servers. However, we remain fully committed to our public servers. Our public servers will offer a larger map, and in the future, we will release different themed seasonal servers, hoping players can create their own stories and destinies there.

Zeverland is available to wishlist now on Steam , where you can also find more information about the game and its dangerously cute world. For the latest news and info, you can follow the game on Instagram , Twitter , TikTok , and Facebook . What are you most excited about in Zeverland? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Is Lanterns Hiding a Major Batman Connection?
articles.summary: We may have yet to meet Batman in the DCU, but one character on Lanterns seemingly shares a major connection to the Dark Knight.
articles.body:
James Gunn and Peter Safran’s DCU may be a couple of years old now, but we still have yet to meet this universe’s version of what is undoubtedly DC’s biggest superhero. Where is the DCU version of Batman? Apart from a quick cameo silhouette seen in the animated series Creature Commandos , we’ve seen neither hide nor hair of the Caped Crusader in the DCU. And it doesn’t appear that’s going to change even with the release of the Clayface movie in October.

While it appears that we’ll have to wait until the long-gestating Batman: The Brave and the Bold comes to fruition to actually meet the DCU’s Batman, there is an interesting Batman universe Easter egg to be found in the HBO series Lanterns . Let’s break down this tease and why it could prove very significant for the DCU as a whole.

The Secret of Kelly Macdonald’s Sheriff Kerry

The show’s unexpected Batman connection centers around Kelly Macdonald’s character, Sheriff Kerry Kane. Kerry is introduced as a foil to Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan, a no-nonsense cop who butts heads with the veteran Green Lantern as he investigates an alien conspiracy in the midst of small-town America. However, it quickly becomes apparent that Sheriff Kane knows a lot more about said conspiracy than she initially lets on. She’s nothing if not a woman with secrets of her own.

One of those secrets seems to involve her previous life as a Gotham City native. Hal brings up the fact that she used to live in Gotham in Episode 2, but Kerry is clearly reluctant to talk about that period of her life. What transpired there and why she decided to relocate to a tiny town in rural Nebraska is something we assume the series will explore before the end of Season 1.

However, it’s not the mere fact that Kerry is a former Gothamite that creates a clear link to Batman; it’s her surname. We eventually learn that her full name is Kerry Kane. Not only is it an alliterative name in the way all superhero love interests seem to be, but the Kane family is one with deep significance in Gotham lore.

Along with the Waynes, the Cobblepots, the Elliots, the Arkhams, and a few others, the Kanes are one of the so-called “First Families of Gotham.” These wealthy families have helped shape Gotham over the centuries, and many retain their power, wealth, and influence even today. In the traditional DC Comics universe, Martha Wayne was originally Martha Kane, and her marriage to Thomas Wayne created a blood link between the Kanes and the Waynes.

Other significant Kane family members include Kathy Kane, who was the original Batwoman in DC’s Silver Age comics and founded the clandestine organization Spyral in the modern comics, and Kate Kane, the current holder of the Batwoman mantle. Kate is actually Bruce Wayne’s cousin, a plot point that factored heavily into The CW’s Batwoman series.

Mind you, Lanterns hasn’t directly confirmed that Kerry Kane is a member of that Kane family, but we find it hard to believe that the writers would just happen to choose that surname and birth city for her without intending it to tie back to the larger Kane family tree. Whatever skeletons Kerry is hiding in her closet, it must be somehow connected to the Kane family’s larger role within the borders of Gotham City. However indirectly, she’s a character with links to Bruce Wayne/Batman himself.

At least until Tom Rhys Harries’ Matt Hagen debuts in Clayface, this makes Sheriff Kerry Kane the character with the closest tangible link to Batman in the DCU. It does highlight one important question, however. So far, apart from the 2026 flash-forward in the pilot and the flashback storyline in Episode 3 , the majority of Lanterns has taken place in the year 2016. Does Batman exist at this point in the DCU timeline? Is he a contemporary of Hal Jordan, or a relatively newer phenomenon like David Corenswet’s Superman (who, don’t forget, went public as a superhero just three years before the events of his first solo film)?

Right now, there’s no way of knowing for sure. Lanterns may reference the existence of Gotham City, but the characters conveniently refrain from acknowledging the Dark Knight himself. It’s entirely possible that Batman hadn’t come onto the scene by the time Kerry made the move from Gotham to Rushville. Even if he had, it may be a case of him being more urban legend than proven reality at that point. Even in 2016, Batman could be a rookie hero just establishing his reputation, if he exists at all.

That said, there’s one piece of evidence to suggest that the DCU may already have a Batman in 2016. We know that Batman: The Brave and the Bold is intended to focus on a relatively older and well-established version of Bruce Wayne. The film is drawing from Grant Morrison’s Batman run, which introduced Damian Wayne (the preteen son of Bruce and Talia al Ghul) as the new Robin. We imagine that means Batman must have been active in the DCU for at least a good 10-15 years by the time The Brave and the Bold rolls around. Both his age and tolerance for brightly clad sidekicks should help set the DCU’s Batman apart from the younger, grittier Dark Knight of Matt Reeves’ films.

Based on that logic, the DCU probably has a Batman by the 2016 setting of Lanterns. Again, he may not be well-established yet, but he’s probably there in some form. Does that mean he’s teamed up with Hal Jordan? Would Chandler’s Hal even tolerate working with a guy dressed like a bat? We have no idea, but that sounds like a story worth exploring.

Do you think Sheriff Kerry Kane is part of Gotham City’s Kane dynasty? Is Batman active in the 2016-era DCU? Let us know your theories in the comments below.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World Has 500 Beasts to Collect, and They're All Super Weird | IGN Preview
articles.summary: So far, Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is shaping up to be another solid and charming entry in the sub-series. The monster-collecting style of RPG is a fairly crowded market these days, but Square Enix's efforts to double down on the charm and wholesomeness of Dragon Quest's world are what make this series so unique and fun to dive into. I had a blast with my limited time with Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World, and I can't wait to see what other oddities and weird creatures to uncover.
articles.body:
The Toriyama art style makes the latest version in this long-running Dragon Quest sub-series instantly appealing.

A staggering 500 collectible monsters left me blown away by the variety and sheer roster size.

Some people in my preview session experienced motion sickness while exploring the world map.

While the core Dragon Quest games are the main draw for many fans of this long-running franchise, the well-established Dragon Quest Monsters sub-series has garnered its own dedicated following since its debut in 1998. Much like its counterpart in the Pokemon series, Square-Enix's monster-collecting RPG is all about capturing Dragon Quest's weirdest critters and training them to be the very best. With the upcoming entry Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World, the sequel is looking to elevate the monster-collectathon and turn-based battle gameplay even further, all channeled into Dragon Quest's stylized, high-fantasy storytelling that's brought to life by the art style of the legendary Akira Toriyama.

At PAX West 2026, we got some hands-on time with Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World, seeing the expanded narrative with multiple protagonists, collecting some of the Dragon Quest franchise's strangest monsters, and adding them to our party. It's so far got the makings of one of the strangest and most expansive entries to date with over 500 monsters to collect -- but above all, it's especially focusing on the heart and plentiful charm that Dragon Quest Monsters is all about.

The Withered World focuses on the further adventures of Bianca and Nera, the returning protagonists from Dragon Quest V, as they embark on a new journey in another realm. After both of their fathers contract a mysterious illness, they find that the only cure is in a new realm known as the Witherwood, which is dealing with its own crisis. After discovering a magical watering tool to help restore sacred trees in the decaying lands, the pair will team with other monster wranglers and gather a massive party of monsters to help bring balance to the realm and save their parents.

What makes the Dragon Quest Monsters sub-series such a well-loved spin-off is that it often goes for a more light-hearted, folksy adventure that's enjoyable for all ages. Moreover, it really leans into the inherent charm and weirdness of the Dragon Quest series by letting you team up with some of the franchise's most bizarre foes. Yes, you can have a party full of the Slime monsters, and that could very well be a powerful team if you power them up well enough.

Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World Screenshots

But what Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World focuses more than other games is the experience of its lead monster wranglers, Bianca and Nera. In contrast to Pokemon, DQ Monsters makes the lead monster wrangler more of a key fixture of the party than previous games, and The Withered World especially does that with both Bianca and Nera having unique perks and favored monster types. This creates more opportunities and benefits for building out specific monster parties for the specific wranglers, especially with Bianca's preference for dragon and beast types.

Though there's more of a narrative following with The Withered World, there's still plenty of time to explore the different zones and build up your party at your leisure. The two areas I got to explore were the starting desert zone around Witherrealm's core kingdom and the tropical island zone with some seriously powerful monsters roaming around. Depending on the protagonist you chose in the beginning, you'll have a party that's built for certain conditions – such as Nera's glasscannon-style build of healing all MP post-battle for magic-focused monsters and resurrecting fallen allies, or Bianca's more brawler build favoring keeping the party's HP topped off and having an easier time bedazzling foes. Still, despite your choices, the protagonists and new monster wranglers will meet up over the course of the adventure and blend their parties.

Much like other DQ Monsters games, battles play out in the familiar turn-based design, with the monster wrangler offering suggestions on targets and specific attacks, using items to heal allies, or even letting the monsters do their own thing with the auto-battle function. It's fairly standard with its approach and execution, but it all makes for a satisfying flow. I especially appreciate the way party composition works. While you can have a party of four mid-sized monsters, bringing in the larger ones will take up more individual slots, making for a smaller party, but a potentially stronger one depending on your chosen wrangler and what their abilities are.

With apparently over 500 collectible monsters to train and evolve, Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is really emphasizing the vast roster of allies to acquire. Even during my limited hands-on time, I was blown away by how much variety there was in the selection of monsters. Also, the designs are so expressive and colorful, which really leans into the Toriyama influence. The core way to expand your party is, of course, through battling and scouting. Depending on the type of monsters, you'll meet certain conditions to be able to scout them in the middle of a fight. If you are stronger than them, or if you've managed to beat them down enough, you can outright recruit them during battle, which will add them to your roster and end the fight.

Along with the familiar beats of battling and collecting monsters, The Withered World also adds the ability to synthesize new ones, essentially merging many of the familiar Dragon Quest monsters into new creations. This is on top of the already large number of base monsters, many of which are spiced versions of existing creatures – such as the Coconut Slime, a more tropical cousin of the enduring Slimes. In my case, I combined a Bantamweight rooster monster with a Platypunk to create a Bullfinch monster, a new powered-up beast that helped add some power to my party.

Unfortunately, one notable issue that came up during previews was that some users might be prone to motion sickness while playing. While I personally didn't experience this, some players in my session and others didn't react well to the visual style of world exploration in particular. This visually interesting world map is presented as a stylized, rolling map that can look a little disruptive to some. Fortunately, the game's accessibility options include ways to ease motion sickness by adjusting the camera and visual effects during exploration.

So far, Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is shaping up to be another solid and charming entry in the sub-series. The monster-collecting style of RPG is a fairly crowded market these days, but Square Enix's efforts to double down on the charm and wholesomeness of Dragon Quest's world are what make this series so unique and fun to dive into. I had a blast with my limited time with Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World, and I can't wait to see what other oddities and weird creatures to uncover.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

articles.title: The Magic of Disney Animation Proves Walt Disney World’s Mission of Thoughtfully Updating its Historical Attractions Is Working
articles.summary: We got an early look at The Magic of Disney Animation at Walt Disney World, and it proves that the theme park's mission of thoughtfully updating its historical attractions is working. Check out our first impressions:
articles.body:
Walt Disney World is gearing up for the biggest expansion of its nearly 55-year history, as it is currently underway in bringing Villains Land, the Cars-themed Piston Peak, Monsters, Inc.’s Monstropolis, and much more to life. However, as exciting as it is to see Disney building new lands, its additional focus and care on revitalizing its beloved yet sometimes outdated historical attractions is what has really surprised me in recent years.

After attending a preview of The Magic of Disney Animation at Hollywood Studios, which will have its grand opening on September 14, I can confidently say this strategy is working and will now have the chance to inspire and create lasting memories for even more guests. Why do I say this? Well, I saw it first-hand (through tears of pride and love) as my 7-year-old son found something more than an attraction running through these halls that once created Lilo & Stitch, Mulan, and Brother Bear.

The Magic of Disney Animation at Walt Disney World's Hollywood Studios

The Magic of Disney Animation Is More Than Just an Attraction

For a bit of context, The Magic of Disney Animation is replacing the derelict Star Wars Launch Bay at Hollywood Studios. It is, in fact, the second iteration of an attraction of the same name that was running during the now–shuttered Walt Disney Feature Animation Florida studio that developed those movies I mentioned earlier and more. Back then, guests could come in and watch animators at work and learn how these Disney films go from an idea in someone’s brain to a global box office success story.

This new take on the attraction has that same mission, even if it's presented in a different way as the studio is no longer there. Inspired by the short ‘Once Upon a Studio’ that was released for The Walt Disney Company’s 100th anniversary in 2023 and featured a nod to every animated film in the studios’ catalog, this is a space where the animators have gone out to lunch and the characters have come to life and are welcoming guests to come in and visit.

Guests can head over to an indoor, air-conditioned Alice in Wonderland-themed playground (with plenty of seating for adults and charging ports!) that is also a loving tribute to the art of Disney Legend Mary Blair, they can watch ‘Once Upon a Studio’ while seeing actual portraits around them come to life and react to what’s happening on screen, and they can meet their favorite characters in spaces inspired by the different stages of animating a film, including Mulan in Story, Rapunzel in Layout, and Stitch in Effects.

However, the one I want to spend a bit more time on is Olaf Draws! This is an experience where an Audio-Animatronics figure of Olaf and on-screen Disney Legends teach you how to draw Mickey, Genie, or even Olaf himself. While it may seem like just a fun excuse to hang out with everyone’s favorite snowman while escaping Florida’s heat, it quickly turned into a core memory as I saw my 7-year-old sit up in his Frozen-style sled and lean into this activity.

I, as the proudest Dad around, saw him take care with every pencil stroke. I saw him make a mistake and get frustrated and learn how to fix it himself. I saw him laugh when Olaf made a funny joke or bantered back and forth with the Legend on screen and, perhaps most importantly, I saw him sign his name and jump up in pride and run to us and show that he brought this character to life on this page. It was a moment I’ll hold in my heart forever.

As parents, all we want in this world is to see our kids soar and reach the stars and find their spark, and, if even for just a moment while being enveloped in Frozen music and a character he loved right in front of him, he found that in this place. This very same place that once housed animators and talented individuals who were working together to share their craft and vision with the world.

The Magic of Disney Animation brings that feeling back to Walt Disney World in a way that I believe has been missing, and it even extends out into the courtyard outside the attraction. The space is modeled after the actual Roy E. Disney Animation Building in Burbank, California, and it has character statues like Pua, Thumper, and Meeko littered about alongside Grauman’s Chinese Theatre-style cement blocks with the hand- or paw-prints of various characters, including Wreck-It Ralph’s that takes up four squares, or Simba’s, who has his paw inside of Mufasa’s.

And that’s not to mention the roaming characters inside and outside of the attraction that may just surprise you and your family. I saw Alice and the Mad Hatter crashing the Unbirthday Party in the playground (to the delight of the children and parents nearby) and videos of Rapunzel playing Duck, Duck, Goose with kids in the courtyard and Pluto posing by a recreation of the iconic Pluto’s Corner street sign that is also found on Disney’s lot.

This, in concert with the Disney music, concept art, historical images, a model Animator’s office with Stitch spinning around in a chair, HeiHei popping out of a trash can, Mushu and Cri-Kee playing Fix-It Felix, and countless nods to Disney history, a museum of sorts where characters have donated items (Maui lent his Fish Hook, Elsa her Orb and Scepter, and much more), there is this sense of legacy and care that just wasn’t present in this way before.

I’m a little worried about capacity and crowd control, as I foresee this being a very popular air-conditioned place to rest, try to meet characters, and let your kids play to their heart’s content at the playground, so I’m hoping everyday guests will be able to experience this place as intended and not as sardines in a tightly packed can.

Disney Is a Carousel of Progress, Not of Standing Still

The Magic of Disney Animation not only shows that care of what came before makes a difference, but that Disney isn’t just prioritizing E-Ticket, mind-blowing experiences at every corner. Listen, this attraction isn’t meant to drive ticket sales through the roof or break new ground in technology, but that doesn’t make it any less of a priority.

I saw a similar notion with Disneyland’s Walt Disney - A Magical Life, which posthumously brought Walt Disney back as an Audio-Animatronics figure to the park he built. Disney (the very-much-alive company, I mean) didn’t have to do this. This attraction, which is literally steps away from the gate where guests walk in, isn’t the most popular or thrilling experience, but it's a tribute to and honor of what came before that stands alongside modern Disney attractions like Rise of the Resistance or the upcoming Avengers: Infinity Defense at Disney California Adventure. It also adds to the experience and didn’t remove the other show that stars an Audio-Animatronics figure of Abraham Lincoln and was one of Walt’s most prized attractions.

It makes for a more complete and meaningful parkgoing experience, and it allows for guests to take home something more than screams of joy and laughter, but also inspiration, hope, and the belief that they too can tell these stories and make their dreams come true.

Walt Disney himself was always about looking forward and immersing families in the stories they love, and he’ll soon also be part of the next big change over at Walt Disney World’s Magic Kingdom, as Carousel of Progress is currently closed and getting its biggest update ever.

Carousel of Progress first debuted at the 1964-1965 New York World’s Fair and looked back 60 years in the past to the turn of century before heading all the way to a glimpse of what the future may hold. The attraction has gone under multiple revisions over the years, but this new iteration that is planned to open in 2027 will bring it forward by decades and add another Walt Disney Audio-Animatronics figure to the intro.

Change can be tough, particularly for a place with as much nostalgia tied to it as a Disney theme park, but after speaking to some of the Imagineers in charge of this project, it’s clear they have a reverence for what Carousel of Progress means to so many guests while also understanding that it doesn’t resonate as much with today’s audience. This new take will start in the late ‘60s and take us through the moon landing, Halloween in the ‘80s, Y2K, and even the far, far future to a look at what life could be like off-planet in an attempt to not only stay relevant for a long time and not feel outdated, but to connect more with guests in 2026 who grew up with the times that will now be shown on stage. It’s also fascinating because it will now look 60 years in the past, just as the original did when it first debuted.

Once again, Disney did not need to do this, but it understands that this attraction, like the company, is a Carousel of Progress and not a Carousel of Standing Still, and it needs to keep innovating and improving what it has so it can meet the guests where they are today and tomorrow and not yesterday.

These examples; Walt Disney - A Magical Life, The Magic of Disney Animation, and the upcoming new iteration of Carousel of Progress, show that honoring your past while also marching forward is a winning combination.

I’ll never forget that night in The Magic of Disney Animation, as I felt the history all around me while seeing our future generation play in a safe space that encouraged creativity and play and left room for the chance to be inspired and realize you are even more talented and wonderful than you may have believed.

We love coming to theme parks for the thrill of the giant drop of a roller coaster or coming face-to-face with our favorite characters or villains, but the true magic of places like these are those moments we don’t plan for. It’s turning a corner to a parade you didn’t know had begun or seeing your daughter in her Elsa dress spin through EPCOT and know that she can be the princess of her own story or watching your son find that he can draw a character he loves on screen and believe that one day he may see his own creation on the big screen or in a park.

These experiences matter and are just as important as the big lands and attractions that draw hours-long lines. These smaller, quieter moments are sometimes the loudest in our lives and can help define who we are, and that’s the real magic of these places and a testament to those who work to keep these experiences ready for the current dreamers of all ages that we hope will one day shape our world for the better.

Adam Bankhurst is a writer for IGN. You can follow him on X/Twitter @AdamBankhurst, Instagram, and TikTok, and listen to his show, Talking Disney Magic.

articles.title: BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony Live Blog: The Future of Warcraft and Diablo Set to Be Revealed Amid StarCraft Rumors
articles.summary: BlizzCon 2026 is upon is, and IGN is reporting live on all the announcements direct from the opening ceremony. Expect big news on everything from World of Warcraft to Diablo, amid strong rumors of a StarCraft announcement.
articles.body:
BlizzCon 2026 is upon is, and IGN is reporting live on all the announcements direct from the opening ceremony.

The company behind Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo, and Overwatch is set to deliver an Opening Ceremony that has more buzz about it than perhaps any BlizzCon in the past. The action kicks off at 10.30am pt / 1.30pm ET / 6.30pm UK time, and we’ll be reporting on all the news from the main stage, where we have reporters on the ground.

So, what can we expect? Blizzard has confirmed that the Opening Ceremony will see Johanna Faries, President of Blizzard Entertainment, joined by leaders of all Blizzard franchises for "major game announcements." The big hope is that Blizzard announces something StarCraft related, after weird glitches were spotted on the official StarCraft website . This clear tease has sent fans of the famous sci-fi real-time strategy series into overdrive, especially with reports indicating Blizzard is working on a StarCraft first-person shooter of some description.

The next major upcoming expansion for World of Warcraft is The Last Titan, which follows the recently released Midnight expansion as the final chapter of the Worldsoul Saga. Will Blizzard tease The Last Titan, or focus more on upcoming content for Midnight?

Expect a star turn from Diablo during the Opening Ceremony. Blizzard has said Diablo "takes center stage to reveal extensive plans for the glorious future of Sanctuary." Could we get a tease for a new Diablo 4 expansion or class?

Overwatch fans, meanwhile, are hoping for news of a new hero, given Blizzard's not yet complete plan to release 10 new heroes this year.

The show itself weighs in at a chunky 75 minutes, so there should be plenty to get fans excited. I’m a huge fan of Blizzard games, especially Warcraft and Diablo, so my hopes are high that we’ll get some big news on both those series in particular. Developer update panels follow the opening ceremony, so deeper dives are coming for hardcore fans to sink their teeth into.

Be sure to check back here for the BlizzCon 2026 opening ceremony live blog, below. While you wait, head to the comments and let us know what you’re hoping to see!

Warcraft card game Hearthstone follows the Diablo 5 announcement with a "pretty epic expansion!" called Black Empire, due out October 20. Blizzard ran through a number of card reveals, and confirmed it's finally putting a narrative into the game. The updated journal launches alongside the Black Empire expansion. 2v2 Hearthstone is coming to the game for the first time, too. But the big news here is the Monk class is coming to Hearthstone in 2027. Expect more on Monk next year.

🐼 🙌 Why do we fight? To just have fun! The new Monk class arrives next year, so keep an eye out for more details as we get closer to release! pic.twitter.com/HBLtm72T1S — Hearthstone (@PlayHearthstone) September 12, 2026

🐼 🙌 Why do we fight? To just have fun! The new Monk class arrives next year, so keep an eye out for more details as we get closer to release! pic.twitter.com/HBLtm72T1S

Blizzard shocked the BlizzCon crowd with the announcement of Diablo 5. We got the debut cinematic, which revolves around the return of The Lord of Terror himself, Diablo, to Sanctuary. "Sanctuary falls," is the tagline. It's out 2029. You enter a world in which Diablo has already won, with no towns or safe places waiting to protect players. "What must you become when the world has already fallen?" is the central question of Diablo 5. Expect more from a Diablo 5 panel later today.

I certainly wasn't expecting a Diablo 5 announcement at Blizzcon, but of course it makes sense that Blizzard is working on a sequel given how successful Diablo 4 has been and continues to be. Diablo 4 launched in June 2023, so Diablo 5 is due to arrive six years later.

Prepare for the next era. Diablo V has been announced. Visit to sign up for future updates. pic.twitter.com/CfO2cyEz0T — Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Prepare for the next era. Diablo V has been announced. Visit to sign up for future updates. pic.twitter.com/CfO2cyEz0T

Diablo 4 Nintendo Switch 2 and content updates announced

BlizzCon continued with a fun Diablo compilation video narrated by Deckard Cain himself.

Thirty years of putting you through Hell and you keep coming back for more. 😈 Here’s to the 30 years of Diablo and the best community alive. For now. pic.twitter.com/ZK9Aab7urd — Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Thirty years of putting you through Hell and you keep coming back for more. 😈 Here’s to the 30 years of Diablo and the best community alive. For now. pic.twitter.com/ZK9Aab7urd

Speaking of Deckard Cain, he leads Diablo 4 players through Season of Hell's Legacy, which sounds like a sort of demonic trip down memory lane in which you fight famous Diablo bosses. It launches on September 15. We also got the announcement of Diablo 4 coming to Nintendo Switch 2 alongside Season of Hell's Legacy.

Also in Diablo news, Spawn - yes, Spawn! - comes to mobile game Diablo Immortal on September 29.

In further Diablo 4 news, the Amazon class is finally coming to the game. She uses a bow and a javeline, and hits the game in the first half of 2027. Expect more from the Diablo 4 What's Next? panel at BlizzCon later this weekend.

Disciplined. Deadly. Legendary. Built on the pillars of an expert soldier, unrivaled athleticism, and mythical magic, the Amazon enters Diablo IV as a new Class Pack in the first half of 2027 🏹 pic.twitter.com/vOmKzu1ChH — Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Disciplined. Deadly. Legendary. Built on the pillars of an expert soldier, unrivaled athleticism, and mythical magic, the Amazon enters Diablo IV as a new Class Pack in the first half of 2027 🏹 pic.twitter.com/vOmKzu1ChH

Aaron Keller from the Overwatch team followed that big StarCraft reveal to talk Overwatch. Doctrine is a vampire support hero who uses bat drones to heal teammates and speed up their attacks. He's coming next month in Season 5, but his limited time Hero Trial kicks off right now and runs until September 14. Expect more information during a BlizzCon panel later this weekend.

Blizzard added that Overwatch Spotlight 2027 will kick off the next chapter in Overwatch's story.

If Doomfist plans to make a new gauntlet, he’s going to need help from a very old friend 🧛 Join him and his allies as they work to break out Doctrine from the depths of Watchpoint: Grimsvotn in our newest Hero Trailer, ‘Breakout.’ pic.twitter.com/MMvH3Gfhe2 — Overwatch (@PlayOverwatch) September 12, 2026

If Doomfist plans to make a new gauntlet, he’s going to need help from a very old friend 🧛 Join him and his allies as they work to break out Doctrine from the depths of Watchpoint: Grimsvotn in our newest Hero Trailer, ‘Breakout.’ pic.twitter.com/MMvH3Gfhe2

Dan Hay, who used to work on Far Cry at Ubisoft, took to the BlizzCon stage to announce the heavily-rumored StarCraft first-person shooter. It's open-world, he confirmed, before declaring: "We are here to reignite this universe... and let's be honest... it's about damn time."

The game's debut cinematic showed Terran Dominion soldiers in training before a battle with the Zerg, which does not go well for our poor recruits. The game is simply titled StarCraft, and it's due out... in 2030! Only a four-year wait then, assuming it's not delayed. We didn't get a look at gameplay, and there are no details at all really other than it's open-world. Given Hay's background with Far Cry, I'm guessing StarCraft will work along the same lines.

So, it's not StarCraft 3, but it is more StarCraft! We've got so many questions. Hopefully BlizzCon answers them.

DEFEND MANKIND. JOIN THE DOMINION. STARCRAFT. 2030. pic.twitter.com/wQwzqYIBmd — STARCRAFT (@StarCraft) September 12, 2026

DEFEND MANKIND. JOIN THE DOMINION. STARCRAFT. 2030. pic.twitter.com/wQwzqYIBmd

Blizzard announced a new animated series for Diablo on Netflix. Faries also teased Overwatch, Warcraft, and "who knows, perhaps even some of our other universes," are set for adaptations. "I promise, as soon as I can, we will share more details with you.

We are thrilled to share that we are in development on a new animated series for Diablo with Netflix. pic.twitter.com/F7dKh73f12 — Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

We are thrilled to share that we are in development on a new animated series for Diablo with Netflix. pic.twitter.com/F7dKh73f12

Heroes of the Storm gets a new character

Blizzard's MOBA, Heroes of the Storm, is coming back in a big way with a new character, Xal'atah, later this month, and another new character is coming at some point afterwards. "Thank you for believing in this game," Faries said. "For carrying that torch. Who knows? We might even have another new hero on the way in the near future. So stay tuned, and we will see you in the Nexus."

BlizzCon 2026 kicks off with flashy cinematic running through all the big games

BlizzCon 2026 has started with a rousing cinematic that runs through all the big hitters. Johanna Faries is on-stage to call it a "special moment for all of us." This is Faries' first BlizzCon as boss of Blizzard, and it sounds like she's close to tears as she praises and thanks her staff. "There's so much going on at Blizzard right now that we couldn't even fit it into this weekend if we tried," she said, perhaps teasing further unnanounced projects.

BlizzCon 2026 starts in five minutes. We're expecting Johanna Faries, President of Blizzard Entertainment, on-stage soon to start the Opening Ceremony. Almost there!

We're taking our seats... and some photos!

With Opening Ceremony now just 30 minutes from kick-off, excitement is building inside Hall D at the Anaheim Convention Center. We're taking our seats now so we can report live from Blizzard's big showcase event. Check out these photos!

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Level-5 Boss Addresses AI Backlash After Fans Hit Out at Game Reveal Showcase
articles.summary: Developer Level-5 has apologized for and explained its use of generative AI after fans spotted 'AI slop' in footage of games like Professor Layton and the Curious Village, DecaPolice, and more.
articles.body:
Developer Level-5 has apologized for and explained its use of generative AI after fans spotted "AI slop" in footage of games like Professor Layton and the Curious Village , DecaPolice, and more.

Concerns emerged following the studio's Nintendo Direct-style presentation earlier this week. Dubbed Level5 Vision 2026 II: Dreams, the show came with first looks at upcoming games, and it also happened to feature what fans suspected to be multiple examples of genAI.

Those who tuned into the 50-minute presentation spent more time talking about what they believed was evidence of AI use rather than the games, such as the Professor Layton remake, Yo-Kai Watch 2: Haunted Domain, and DecaPolice. The footage causing a stir is mostly limited to background scenes, but it's the fact that fans had to question Level-5 in the first place that's turned the situation into a full-fledged controversy for the Japan-based studio.

Oh no Level-5 is DEFINATELY using Gen AI to "update" Professor Layton. Especially when you compare the original backgrounds to the new. So many weird details and inconsistencies were added. pic.twitter.com/0tRQ9vKn03 — AmericanYoshi (@AmericanYoshi) September 10, 2026

Oh no Level-5 is DEFINATELY using Gen AI to "update" Professor Layton. Especially when you compare the original backgrounds to the new. So many weird details and inconsistencies were added. pic.twitter.com/0tRQ9vKn03

⁉️ Dans le nouveau trailer de Yo-kai Watch 2 : Haunted Domain, Nathan a… changé de visage ?! 😭 #YOKAIWATCH Hier (gauche) / Aujourd’hui (droite) pic.twitter.com/Vr3rzwNPA7 — Yo-net Watch (@YonetWatch) September 10, 2026

⁉️ Dans le nouveau trailer de Yo-kai Watch 2 : Haunted Domain, Nathan a… changé de visage ?! 😭 #YOKAIWATCH Hier (gauche) / Aujourd’hui (droite) pic.twitter.com/Vr3rzwNPA7

"I was SO excited when Level-5 announced their big comeback with Professor Layton, Decapolice, Yo-Kai Watch, and more," one fan on X/Twitter said . "But seeing this much blatant genAI being used across their games… yeah, this ain’t it"

"You were a beautiful studio," another fan said . "Now you are nothing more than a disappointment to us. We don’t want this AI s**t."

Level-5 president and CEO Akihiro Hino, who also hosted the showcase with his own animated avatar, took to X/Twitter to calm the noise. His message was both an apology and an explanation, confirming that Level-5 did, in fact, use generative AI for some aspects of development.

Hino described Level-5's heavy use of AI as "experimentation with the latest technology," adding that the team "sincerely apologizes to anyone who found this off-putting."

I was excited about Decapolice but Level-5 AI use is disgusting to me. I can't support that. — Kabi (@KabiPlays) September 10, 2026

I was excited about Decapolice but Level-5 AI use is disgusting to me. I can't support that.

"However, please be assured that all elements defining the appeal and individuality of our released titles— such as the scenario, character designs, and foundational settings — are created entirely by human hands," Hino said (via Google translate). "We utilize AI primarily to streamline the process of digitizing human-created assets; for instance, accurately converting original artwork into 3D polygon models. You can rest assured that the games we release do not contain content simply generated by AI."

Hino also defended how Level-5 has used AI so far, saying: "the time saved through AI-driven efficiencies has allowed our creators to dedicate more of their efforts to the true essence of creativity." For him and the rest of the team, the belief is that the finished versions of games like Professor Layton and the Curious Village will still please fans in the end. Part of the reason it leaned so heavily on genAI this time around was so it could shrink "the development cycle for major titles from the current five years down to two."

"That said, we cannot deny that we made extensive use of AI this time, driven by a desire to deliver a presentation that was visually striking and easy to grasp," he continued. "We will take this experience as a learning opportunity for the future, so please look forward to Level-5’s next presentation."

pic.twitter.com/cict4COGTP — ⬡ Nectur Bee ⬢ (@NecturBee) September 12, 2026

It's an explanation that hasn't gone over well in the Level-5 community. Replies to the post include fans still concerned about generative technology being used during development at all, fearing that affected games will be forever tarnished.

"Generative AI is trained on the stolen works of countless artists by tech companies to profit off their work, with the intent of replacing artists," one popular reply said . "By using it you replaced artists. You're profiting off of the skill of artists whose work has been stolen to power this software."

"I believe the human heart matters more than speed to market; surely it is better to take five years without using AI," another post written in Japanese said (via Google Translate). "If even a single asset is created using AI, the nagging worry — 'Is this image, piece of music, or line of dialogue made by AI or a human?' — would never go away. Isn't preserving that trust the most important thing?"

Hino didn't offer a specific game plan when it comes to how Level-5 will tweak its development plans going forward. For now, Professor Layton and the Curious Village, a remake of the original 2007 game, is slated to come to PC and consoles in 2027 . Another new game in the series, the New World of Steam , is due out this December.

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: T-Mobile's Apple iPhone 18 Pro "On Us" Deal Explained
articles.body:
Apple's newest lineup of iPhone 18 phones, which includes the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the all new iPhone 18 Duo, was announced during Apple's "Surprise and Shine" Event on September 9. Preorders have officially gone live for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, with orders shipping out starting September 18.

Get an iPhone 18 Pro "On Us" at T-Mobile

Preorders are now live, phones ship on September 18

Get an Apple iPhone 18 Pro "On Us" at T-Mobile

T-Mobile has kicked off its iPhone 18 "On Us" promotion, which gives you a free iPhone 18 Pro phone when you either switch carriers and port in your number or trade in an eligible phone in any condition. You'll also have to sign up for the Experience Beyond plan, with the discount applied as bill credits over a 36 month period for a total of $1,199 in credit. There is a one-time $35 connection charge.

Alternatively, you can preorder the iPhone 18 Pro Max and get the same $1,199 in bill credits. The Pro Max costs $1,299 retail, which means you'll have to pay an extra $100, still worth it if you want to upgrade to a larger screen size.

The Experience Beyond plan costs $100 per month for a single line with AutoPay (plus taxes and fees). The plan gives you unlimited talk, text, and 5G premium data. Other perks include Netflix (Standard with ads) and Hulu subscriptions, Apple TV for $3/mo, unlimited mobile hotspot, T-Satellite, phone upgrade eligibility every year, and a 5 year price guarantee. International travelers can also benefit from unlimited text and 30GB of high-speed data in Canada and Mexico and unlimited text and 15GB of high-speed data in over 215 other countries.

So far only the iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max are eligible, but the iPhone Duo may follow

Currently the only promotion listed is for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. There's a good chance, however, that we'll see a similar discount or better for the iPhone Duo. The iPhone Duo would be an especially attractive offer, since the phone will carry a sticker price of $1,999 . We'll find out when the iPhone Duo goes up for preorder on October 16.

Usually with these types of promotions you end up paying more for the phone compared to buying it outright, but who wants to spend that much money right out of the gate for a phone? If you intend to stick with T-Mobile's 5G network anyways, then that's all the more reason to start using Apple's new iPhone immediately.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable phone, the rest are incremental upgrades

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max upgrades the APU to the new Apple A20 Pro processor built on a new 2-nanometer process technology. Apple claims 40% greater graphics performanceo ver the previous iPhone. Other notable upgrades include a main camera that's now equipped with variable aperture from f/1.48 to f/4.0 and faster 60W charging.

The iPhone Duo will be a foldable smartphone with two displays: a 5.4" screen when the phone is folded and a larger 7.6" screen when it's unfolded. This will be Apple's thinnest iPhone ever (in unfolded mode). It will be equipped with the same Apple A20 Pro processor found in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

articles.title: Borderlands 4 DLC Character and Free-to-Play Weekend Attract Resurgence on Steam
articles.summary: Borderlands 4 is climbing Steam charts as players fall head over heels for its new DLC character – a Vault Hunter named Loveless the Hacker.
articles.body:
Borderlands 4 is climbing Steam charts as players fall head over heels for its new DLC character – a Vault Hunter named Loveless the Hacker.

Gearbox Software's latest Borderlands game struggled in the months following its September 2025 launch. Despite delivering the looter shooter series' biggest launch ever , technical issues across PC and console , as well as Gearbox's handling of the situation , were immediately followed by a steep decline in players, with SteamDB recording numbers that have struggled to break 10,000 concurrent users since January of this year.

Borderlands 4 might have launched to generally favorable reviews (IGN gave it an 8/10 ), but it's struggled to recapture player interest – until now. Thursday, September 10, saw the release of Loveless the Hacker, a DLC character with high-end cybernetics. She's only a small part of a grander Story Pack 2 release, and she seems to be giving the game a second wind.

"Two minds exist inside Loveless, forming a synchronized set of lethal skills that strike as one," a description for Loveless says. "Through a symbiotic melding of the biological and digital, this ex-Anshin hacker-turned-assassin has become a superior lifeform. Equipped with the highest-end cybernetics, Loveless shares her psyche with a digital virus of her own creation, which can digistruct into a physical Wyrm form to act as a deadly extension of her shared, perfection-seeking will."

At the time of this story's publication, Borderlands 4 is enjoying around 26,000 concurrent players on Steam alone. That's the most it's had since November 2025, and far higher than the 17,000-player peak it reached with the launch of Story Pack 1 in March. The base game has also now managed to round out the Top 5 sellers on Steam in the U.S., and it's even come in at nine in the Top 10 global list.

Player counts also appear to be climbing even further, with those in its Steam reviews section specifically calling attention to Loveless as the reason they've decided to return to the planet Kairos. Many refer to voice acting from actress Carin Gilfry as a specific positive, but you can probably guess what a lot of the others had to say.

"Bought the game solely because of Loveless," one review said . "This is how you market."

Bro she’s so bad Loveless? But girl I LOVE YOU pic.twitter.com/ASqXkrZhhX — Ccrypto (@Ccrypto5) September 3, 2026

Bro she’s so bad Loveless? But girl I LOVE YOU pic.twitter.com/ASqXkrZhhX

"Actually a nice character," a popular review said . "Looks good, good design, is insanely OP (can solo bosses without any help). But her alternate heads are a bit -- meh. And she costs $9.99. The VA put some effort into it though. Overall – I think she fits."

"Letting me buy the Vault Hunter without having to by the DLC story pack is the correct call," another fan said , referencing Loveless' $10 asking price compared to the recently released Story Pack 2 expansion. "Glad they learned. Also, step on me Mommy."

There are a number of factors contributing to Borderlands 4's boost in players on Steam, specifically. In addition to Loveless' status as a popular addition, Story Pack 2: FL4K and the Last Resort has also helped. There's also the fact that Gearbox is in the middle of a 50% off sale, bringing its price to $34.99 in the midst of a free-to-play weekend that runs until September 14.

It's unclear if the numbers will stick, but it seems to be a winning weekend for Borderlands 4 nonetheless. articles.title: Heroes of the Storm Gets First New Character in Six Years
articles.summary: Announced at Blizzcon 2026, Heroes of the Storm is getting its first new character since Hogger was released in 2020, as well as a new PTR.
articles.body:
Blizzard’s flagship MOBA, Heroes of the Storm , is finally showing signs of life.

Announced at Blizzcon 2026, the game is getting its first new character since Hogger was released in 2020, as well as a new PTR.

Xal'atath, the primary antagonist of World of Warcraft ’s Midnight expansion, is coming to the Nexus on Monday, September 28. The PTR begins on Monday, September 14.

This is a welcome surprise for Heroes of the Storm fans, who had all but accepted that the game might never get updated again. Blizzard ended official support for HotS in 2022, explaining that “future patches will primarily focus on client sustainability and bug fixing, with balance updates coming as needed."

However, the title received a significant patch in 2023, with smaller, sporadic changes and new skins trickling through in the years since then. Fans are more hopeful than ever, and Blizzard is, too — but future updates all depend on how the community responds to this fresh breath of air.

Speaking to the media, a Blizzard franchise leader said the company will “see how this does,” revealing that “if the community responds well, it could lead to more things” and describing this update as the "first foray into something really big.”

An animated Diablo show is in the works at Netflix, as announced at Blizzcon 2026, and there could be more to come.

Blizzard president Johanna Faries revealed the news, alongside a teaser for future series based on some of the company's other properties.

"We are thrilled to share that we are in development for a new animated series for Diablo with Netflix," she told the crowd. "As a big Diablo player myself, and someone who loves the indulgent darkness of Sanctuary, I am very excited to see this project come to life. It's just the beginning; to our Overwatch community, to our Warcraft community, and who knows — perhaps even some of our other universes, just know there are great discussions being had.

"And while I begged and pleaded to be able to share more, I can’t spill the beans just yet. I promise, as soon as we can, we will share more details with you."

We are thrilled to share that we are in development on a new animated series for Diablo with Netflix. pic.twitter.com/F7dKh73f12

"After decades of bringing entire universes to life through our games, we’re partnering with some creative powerhouses to tell even more stories beyond gaming across new screens," Blizzard said in a press release. "A new animated series set in the world of Diablo is in development with Netflix. More details will be shared in the future, but this is only the beginning, with even more taking shape across our universes."

A slew of other big reveals were announced for the franchise at Blizzcon, the biggest of which was the reveal of Diablo 5 , set to release in Spring 2029. This game takes place after Sanctuary has fallen, where our big bad, Diablo himself, has won.

"For the first time, you won't be fighting to stop Diablo for taking Sanctuary. You'll enter a world where he already has. There are no towns or safe places to protect you. ...what must you become when the world has already fallen?" Blizzard franchise leaders said during the Saturday showcase.

articles.title: Next StarCraft Game Announced at BlizzCon as an Open-World Shooter, but It’s Not Due Out Until 2030
articles.summary: It’s been over 15 years since Blizzard’s beloved real-time strategy game, StarCraft 2, came out. Now, a new game in the series has been announced — but it’s still years away.
articles.body:
It’s been over 15 years since Blizzard’s beloved real-time strategy game, StarCraft 2 , came out. Now, a new game in the series has been announced — but it’s still years away.

Revealed at BlizzCon 2026, the simply named StarCraft is the next title in the sci-fi franchise, and it’s going to look markedly different from its predecessors.

In fact, it’s a completely different genre. StarCraft is an open-world shooter, and it’s due out in 2030. While this distant launch window makes it hard to get too excited about StarCraft just yet, Blizzard has a history of announcing games far before they're ready for the public to play. In fact, it’s something the company behind Warcraft, Diablo, and Overwatch is notorious for doing, historically touting the mantra: “It’ll be ready when it’s ready.”

The announcement of a new StarCraft game was expected at BlizzCon, after the official StarCraft website became rife with visual ‘glitches,’ and issued a ‘warning’ telling users their device has been “compromised.” Fans took this to mean that a big update for the franchise was on the horizon, and they were right.

Indeed, rumors of a StarCraft shooter had been circling for years. In 2024, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier told IGN’s Podcast Unlocked about Blizzard’s third attempt at developing a StarCraft shooter with former Far Cry executive producer Dan Hay, who joined Blizzard in 2022, leading the charge. Then, later in 2024, a job posting was listed for an ‘upcoming open-world shooter’ that fans were certain was tied to this StarCraft game.

Blizzard has had a tough time developing StarCraft shooters over the years. StarCraft Ghost , announced in 2002, was going to be a tactical-action console game in which you played as a deadly Ghost operative in the employ of the Dominion, but it was canceled in 2006 after a series of delays.

A second attempt to make a StarCraft shooter, codenamed Ares, was canceled in 2019 so Blizzard could focus on Diablo 4 and Overwatch 2 . Ares was reportedly “like Battlefield in the StarCraft universe,” but, like Ghost, fell by the wayside.

Now, it’s a case of third time lucky for Blizzard with this new StarCraft shooter in development. Check out everything announced at BlizzCon 2026 for all the news from across Blizzard.

articles.title: X-Men Star Inde Navarrette Teases Her Plan to Nail Rogue’s Southern Accent
articles.summary: Obsession breakout Inde Navarrette already has a plan to make sure she nails Rogue's iconic Southern accent in the new X-Men movie.
articles.body:
Obsession breakout Inde Navarrette already has a plan to make sure she nails Rogue's iconic Southern accent in the new X-Men movie .

Navarrette will jump from horror to the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) when she appears in X-Men in 2028. As revealed last month, it's due out May 5, 2028, but even more than Rogue's power-stealing abilities and fierce attitude, fans have been dying to know if Navarrette will bring any spice to Rogue's voice.

The character is known for her southern draw, especially thanks to the delivery made popular by original X-Men animated series voice actress Lenore Zann . Navarrette may not have the natural accent audiences would expect from Rogue, but she told Entertainment Tonight that the mutant team member's voice is very much already on her mind.

"I've never told this publicly – I completely forgot – but I have a divorced family. I grew up in Texas for a good majority of my life," Navarrette said when asked how she'll build Rogue's voice. "So, honestly, those Southern women are really my favorite."

Navarrette then noted her specific connection to Corpus Christi, a coastal town located toward the south end of Texas. For the Obsession actress-turned-Marvel superhero, it's the "old Southern women" that she "really, really loves." But her appreciation for the South doesn't stop there.

"But, specifically, Mississippi – Rogue is from Mississippi," she continued. "So, I really just want to go there. I wanna really do her justice."

Navarrette is just one piece of a grander MCU puzzle. Also confirmed for the big MCU X-Men reboot movie are Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost. Gen V and Scream 7 star Asa Germann was also recently picked to play the winged mutant, Angel .

So many other pieces need to come together before X-Men arrives, but director Jake Schreier has teased a team-up movie worth waiting for. In August, he talked about some of the comic books he's looking to for inspiration , promising to give MCU fans a movie that is a "new spin" on what they've seen with past live-action X-Men films. Meanwhile, Navarrette is reportedly so excited to do the movie that she passed up a part in Heat 2 .
